title: Impact of School District Boundaries on Urban House Prices

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
**Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD)** - This is appropriate because school district boundaries create a sharp discontinuity where houses on one side are assigned to a different district than houses on the other side. The key assumption is that houses just on either side of the boundary are similar in all unobservable characteristics except for school district assignment, making the boundary assignment quasi-random.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(rdrobust)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s94_data.csv")

# Create proper running variable (distance from boundary with sign)
# Negative values for control district, positive for treated district
data$running_var_signed <- ifelse(data$treated == 1, data$running_var, -data$running_var)

# Main RDD analysis using rdrobust
rdd_result <- rdrobust(y = data$y, 
                      x = data$running_var_signed, 
                      c = 0)

# Print main results
cat("=== MAIN RDD RESULTS ===\n")
cat("RDD Coefficient (Treatment Effect):", round(rdd_result$coef[1], 4), "\n")
cat("Standard Error:", round(rdd_result$se[1], 4), "\n")
cat("P-value:", round(rdd_result$pv[1], 4), "\n")
cat("95% Confidence Interval: [", round(rdd_result$ci[1,1], 4), ", ", round(rdd_result$ci[1,2], 4), "]\n")
cat("Bandwidth used:", round(rdd_result$bws[1], 4), "\n")
cat("Number of observations:", rdd_result$N[1] + rdd_result$N[2], "\n")

# Robustness check 1: Different bandwidth (half of optimal)
rdd_robust1 <- rdrobust(y = data$y, 
                       x = data$running_var_signed, 
                       c = 0,
                       h = rdd_result$bws[1] * 0.5)

cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECK 1: Half Bandwidth ===\n")
cat("RDD Coefficient:", round(rdd_robust1$coef[1], 4), "\n")
cat("P-value:", round(rdd_robust1$pv[1], 4), "\n")

# Robustness check 2: Different bandwidth (double optimal)
rdd_robust2 <- rdrobust(y = data$y, 
                       x = data$running_var_signed, 
                       c = 0,
                       h = rdd_result$bws[1] * 2)

cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECK 2: Double Bandwidth ===\n")
cat("RDD Coefficient:", round(rdd_robust2$coef[1], 4), "\n")
cat("P-value:", round(rdd_robust2$pv[1], 4), "\n")

# Robustness check 3: Different polynomial order
rdd_robust3 <- rdrobust(y = data$y, 
                       x = data$running_var_signed, 
                       c = 0,
                       p = 2)

cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECK 3: Quadratic Polynomial ===\n")
cat("RDD Coefficient:", round(rdd_robust3$coef[1], 4), "\n")
cat("P-value:", round(rdd_robust3$pv[1], 4), "\n")

# Summary statistics by treatment status
cat("\n=== DESCRIPTIVE STATISTICS ===\n")
cat("Mean log house price in better district (control):", 
    round(mean(data$y[data$treated == 0]), 4), "\n")
cat("Mean log house price in worse district (treated):", 
    round(mean(data$y[data$treated == 1]), 4), "\n")
cat("Raw difference:", 
    round(mean(data$y[data$treated == 1]) - mean(data$y[data$treated == 0]), 4), "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a **negative coefficient** of approximately **-0.10 to -0.25** (10-25% decrease in house prices). Being in a less desirable school district should reduce property values because:

1. Parents value school quality and are willing to pay premium for better schools
2. School district quality affects neighborhood desirability and future resale value
3. The RDD estimate should be smaller in magnitude than the raw difference since it controls for other neighborhood characteristics that vary with distance from boundary

The effect should be statistically significant given that school quality is a major factor in residential location decisions, especially for families with children.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: The identification strategy leverages the discontinuity at the school district boundary.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Houses in the less desirable school district exhibit lower log prices.
